distractors: Digging a canal around the forts over two years
Persuading the forts to surrender without a shot
Landing an army that marched overland from Texas
questions.explanation: After days of mortar bombardment failed, Farragut's wooden ships charged past the forts in the dark on April 24, 1862, beat a small Confederate river fleet, and anchored off New Orleans. The Confederacy's largest city and port fell barely a year into the war.

It held the Confederacy's only army headquarters
It was where all Confederate cotton was stored
questions.explanation: New Orleans was the South's biggest city, a major shipbuilding and banking center, and the mouth of its greatest river. From that base, Union forces could push upriver toward Vicksburg and Port Hudson and occupy Louisiana's richest sugar parishes within months.

questions.question: The Siege of Port Hudson ended in July 1863. Why did the Confederate garrison finally surrender?

A hurricane destroyed the fortifications
They ran out of drinking water in one week

They left voting rights completely unchanged
